text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 1.2% today as oil prices rose on geopolitical tension: the U.S. attacked Iran's Larak Island, prompting Iranian retaliation against American bases in Jordan, and Trump pledged a harder response. Crude oil moved up in response to the escalation risk—U.S. oil traded at $83.90 per barrel today—and refineries are running at 97.4% capacity, meaning higher oil prices directly support refinery margins and profitability.

The stock has climbed 4.2% over two weeks as these Middle East tensions have built. Separately, news of a major U.S. oil deal with Venezuela and broader geopolitical friction with Russia add to the sense of oil supply uncertainty, which typically benefits refiners by widening the spread between crude prices and refined product sales.
